question.problem: An angle $\theta $ in the coordinate plane (measured in the usual way) has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={20}^{∘}.$ Which of the following cannot be $\theta ?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's remind ourselves of the relationship between ${\theta }_{R}$ and $\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225277/assets/a2d02d14edf25a59eceb842a2cc902f07a29754f0978ec56a8293e16698ec383.png)

Using ${\theta }_{R}={20}^{∘},$ let's calculate all possible values of $\theta .$

- If $\theta $ lies in the first quadrant, then $\theta ={\theta }_{R}={20}^{∘}.$

- If $\theta $ lies in the second quadrant, then $\theta ={180}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R}={180}^{∘}-{20}^{∘}={160}^{∘}.$

- If $\theta $ lies in the third quadrant, then $\theta ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R}={180}^{∘}+{20}^{∘}={200}^{∘}.$

- If $\theta $ lies in the fourth quadrant, then $\theta ={360}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R}={360}^{∘}-{20}^{∘}={340}^{∘}.$

Therefore, $\theta $ cannot be equal to ${260}^{∘}.$
